scope_note: Verified rolling radar for 2024-10-12 through 2026-10-12, plus separately labelled anchors; not a completeness claim.

papers.title: Lunar rock investigation and tri-aspect characterization of lunar farside regolith by a digital twin
papers.why: Mission teams need to evaluate rover mobility and science operations despite uncertain lunar terrain properties.
papers.how: Couples reconstructed local terrain, Yutu-2 dynamics, terramechanics, shared commands, and mission-data updates in a digital twin.
papers.what: Demonstrates an operational perception-physics-decision loop on farside mission data.
papers.transfer: Anchor architecture for closing the loop from reconstruction to mobility prediction and model correction.
papers.limitation: Mission-specific modeling and uncertain regolith parameters limit broad generalization.

papers.title: Adapting Stereo Vision From Objects To 3D Lunar Surface Reconstruction with the StereoLunar Dataset
papers.why: Terrestrial stereo foundation models degrade under low texture, extreme lighting, and lunar descent geometry.
papers.how: Uses physically rendered South-Pole stereo supervision and fine-tunes MASt3R across altitude, illumination, and trajectory variation.
papers.what: Provides a public lunar stereo benchmark and evidence that domain-specific adaptation improves geometry and pose estimation.
papers.transfer: Direct blueprint for adapting DUSt3R/MASt3R/VGGT-class models to planetary imagery.
papers.limitation: Synthetic-to-real transfer remains constrained by simulator fidelity and limited real ground truth.

papers.title: High-Resolution and Spatial-Continuous 3-D Model Reconstruction of Martian Surface by Integrating Multisensor Data of Zhurong Rover
papers.why: Rover-scale Martian models need both local detail and spatial continuity for science and operations.
papers.how: Integrates multiple Zhurong rover sensor products into a high-resolution continuous surface model.
papers.what: Shows a mission-data path from heterogeneous observations to coherent Martian terrain reconstruction.
papers.transfer: Useful real-data target for testing neural reconstruction and uncertainty-aware fusion.
papers.limitation: This seed record was verified at metadata level; inspect the full paper before extracting quantitative claims.

papers.title: A physics-based sensor simulation environment for lunar ground operations
papers.why: Lunar perception testing needs visual effects generated by low-angle illumination, reflectance, dust, and terrain interaction.
papers.how: Combines Chrono deformable-terrain dynamics with ray tracing, Hapke photometry, and VIPER/RASSOR digital twins.
papers.what: Produces coupled sensor and interaction simulation suitable for perception and in-silico operations studies.
papers.transfer: Ideal base for reconstruction domain randomization tied to physical nuisance parameters.
papers.limitation: The published study demonstrates simulated VIPER and RASSOR cases; quantitative synthetic-to-real perception validation remains limited.

papers.title: LuSNAR: A Lunar Segmentation, Navigation and Reconstruction Dataset based on Muti-sensor for Autonomous Exploration
papers.why: Lunar autonomy lacks multi-task benchmarks connecting perception, reconstruction, and navigation.
papers.how: Builds nine Unreal/AirSim lunar scenes with stereo, depth, LiDAR, semantic labels, and rover poses.
papers.what: Provides a reusable simulated benchmark spanning segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and navigation.
papers.transfer: Good seed for joint metrics and pretraining, including later global localization work.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint and synthetic benchmark; realism and transfer require independent testing.

papers.title: CLVSim: A comprehensive framework for crewed lunar vehicle simulation—Modeling and applications
papers.why: Crewed lunar mobility needs system-level simulation beyond isolated wheel tests.
papers.how: Integrates SPH soft terrain, suspension, motors, wheels, fenders, and driver subsystems.
papers.what: Demonstrates a high-fidelity framework for mechanism and dust-related design studies.
papers.transfer: Supports co-design of vehicle mechanics, perception placement, and control.
papers.limitation: Vehicle-specific fidelity and computational cost may hinder large policy-learning sweeps.

papers.title: A Study Demonstrating That Using Gravitational Offset to Prepare Extraterrestrial Mobility Missions Is Misleading
papers.why: Earth tests with simple gravity offsets can misrepresent extraterrestrial rover mobility.
papers.how: Validates CPU/GPU co-simulation of multibody rover dynamics and continuum granular terrain against experiments, then changes gravity in simulation.
papers.what: Argues for physics-based scaling and exposes a validation trap in low-gravity mission preparation.
papers.transfer: Sets a strong validation standard for lunar/Mars digital twins and learned dynamics models.
papers.limitation: Moon predictions cannot be directly validated without lunar ground-truth mobility data.

papers.title: DUSt3R: Geometric 3D Vision Made Easy
papers.why: Classical multi-stage reconstruction is brittle when cameras are uncalibrated or unposed.
papers.how: Regresses dense point maps with a transformer and globally aligns pairwise reconstructions.
papers.what: Unifies depth, pose, matching, and dense reconstruction in a learned feed-forward geometry paradigm.
papers.transfer: Foundation for planetary domain adaptation under unusual lighting and view geometry.
papers.limitation: Terrestrial training priors and compute demands require planetary calibration and onboard study.

papers.title: Grounding Image Matching in 3D with MASt3R
papers.why: Image matching is geometrically 3D but usually optimized as a separate 2D task.
papers.how: Adds dense local descriptors and fast reciprocal matching to DUSt3R point-map regression.
papers.what: Improves robust matching under large viewpoint changes and supports map-free localization.
papers.transfer: Directly relevant to lunar stereo, descent imagery, and cross-view rover localization.
papers.limitation: Still requires domain adaptation for low-texture, harsh-illumination planetary imagery.

papers.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
papers.why: Specialized 3D tasks and iterative post-processing impede simple, fast reconstruction pipelines.
papers.how: Uses a large transformer to predict cameras, depth, point maps, and point tracks from many views in one forward pass.
papers.what: Establishes a versatile visual-geometry foundation model and backbone for downstream tasks.
papers.transfer: Promising base for one-model planetary perception, if uncertainty and domain shift are addressed.
papers.limitation: Full attention and terrestrial supervision raise scalability, calibration, and onboard deployment concerns.

papers.title: FlashVGGT: Efficient and Scalable Visual Geometry Transformers with Compressed Descriptor Attention
papers.why: Global attention makes visual-geometry transformers expensive on long sequences.
papers.how: Compresses each frame into descriptor tokens and uses chunk-recursive cached attention.
papers.what: Scales feed-forward reconstruction to thousands of images with much lower inference cost.
papers.transfer: Targets the long-traverse and onboard-compute bottleneck in planetary mapping.
papers.limitation: Planetary performance and uncertainty under extreme appearance shift remain untested.

papers.title: Gaussian Splatting SLAM
papers.why: Robots need online maps that support tracking, geometry, and high-fidelity rendering.
papers.how: Optimizes camera motion directly against incremental 3D Gaussians with geometric verification and regularization.
papers.what: Shows live monocular Gaussian mapping that unifies representation across core SLAM functions.
papers.transfer: Candidate representation for rover digital twins and operator visualization.
papers.limitation: Photometric optimization can be brittle under planetary lighting changes and resource limits.

papers.title: SplaTAM: Splat Track & Map 3D Gaussians for Dense RGB-D SLAM
papers.why: Dense robot maps need explicit volumetric support for localization and reconstruction.
papers.how: Tracks and expands a 3D Gaussian map from an unposed RGB-D stream using silhouette-based density cues.
papers.what: Demonstrates high-fidelity dense RGB-D SLAM with explicit Gaussians.
papers.transfer: Useful hybrid baseline when rover depth or LiDAR is available.
papers.limitation: Relies on RGB-D-style sensing and benchmarks unlike dusty, outdoor planetary scenes.

papers.title: Photo-SLAM: Real-time Simultaneous Localization and Photorealistic Mapping for Monocular, Stereo, and RGB-D Cameras
papers.why: Neural photorealistic SLAM often cannot run on portable robot hardware.
papers.how: Combines explicit geometric features with implicit photometric features and progressive Gaussian-pyramid training.
papers.what: Runs multiple camera configurations in real time, including an embedded Jetson platform demonstration.
papers.transfer: Strong onboard baseline for geometry/rendering trade-offs in rover systems.
papers.limitation: Planetary illumination and outdoor-scale robustness are not established by indoor benchmarks.

papers.title: MISO: Multiresolution Submap Optimization for Efficient Globally Consistent Neural Implicit Reconstruction
papers.why: Large-scale neural SLAM struggles with backend cost and global consistency.
papers.how: Uses learned multiresolution implicit submaps with hierarchical local optimization and global alignment/fusion.
papers.what: Improves efficiency and accuracy for large neural SDF reconstructions.
papers.transfer: Relevant to long rover traverses and map correction under bounded memory.
papers.limitation: Needs planetary-scale outdoor and onboard-compute evaluation.

papers.title: PINGS: Gaussian Splatting Meets Distance Fields within a Point-Based Implicit Neural Map
papers.why: Robots need maps that are both photorealistic and metrically/geometrically useful.
papers.how: Unifies LiDAR-derived distance fields and camera-derived Gaussian radiance fields in elastic neural points.
papers.what: Builds large-scale, globally consistent maps with mutual geometric and photometric improvement.
papers.transfer: Best seed for a rover map joining perception, geometry, rendering, and downstream traversal.
papers.limitation: Urban LiDAR-visual data do not reproduce planetary appearance, terrain, or resource constraints.

papers.title: GauSS-MI: Gaussian Splatting Shannon Mutual Information for Active 3D Reconstruction
papers.why: Active reconstruction needs next-best views that account for visual-model uncertainty.
papers.how: Models per-Gaussian uncertainty and scores viewpoints with Shannon mutual information inside a motion-planning system.
papers.what: Improves reconstruction visual quality and acquisition efficiency in simulated and real scenes.
papers.transfer: Can be extended to rover view planning with hazard, energy, and science-value utilities.
papers.limitation: Visual quality is not yet equivalent to safe or scientifically valuable planetary mapping.

papers.title: Robot Learning with Super-Linear Scaling
papers.why: Real robot data collection does not scale favorably with human effort.
papers.how: CASHER crowdsources reconstructed digital twins, learns in simulation, and amortizes demonstrations as policy competence grows.
papers.what: Shows zero/few-shot real-to-sim-to-real scaling across real tasks and video-scan adaptation.
papers.transfer: Suggests scalable training from analogue-site or mission-scene reconstructions.
papers.limitation: Planetary terrain physics, communication delay, and safety make transfer harder than indoor manipulation.

papers.title: Demonstrating GPU Parallelized Robot Simulation and Rendering for Generalizable Embodied AI with ManiSkill3
papers.why: Robot learning needs fast parallel physics, rendering, diverse tasks, and digital twins.
papers.how: Runs GPU-parallel simulation/rendering with heterogeneous environments, point clouds, voxels, and large demonstrations.
papers.what: Provides a high-throughput embodied-AI simulator spanning many task families and digital twins.
papers.transfer: Architecture inspiration for scalable rover perception/control training, not a ready lunar simulator.
papers.limitation: Contact/terrain and sensor models require domain-specific planetary extensions.

papers.title: RoboSpatial: Teaching Spatial Understanding to 2D and 3D Vision-Language Models for Robotics
papers.why: General vision-language data underrepresent reference frames and robot-relevant spatial relationships.
papers.how: Pairs egocentric images with 3D scans and large-scale spatial-relation annotations for 2D/3D model training.
papers.what: Improves affordance and spatial-relation tasks relevant to robotic manipulation.
papers.transfer: Motivates lunar datasets encoding rover-, world-, orbital-, and object-centric frames plus terrain affordances.
papers.limitation: Indoor/tabletop semantics and manipulation do not directly address unstructured planetary terrain.

papers.title: WildGS-SLAM: Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM in Dynamic Environments
papers.why: Dynamic content corrupts monocular tracking and dense reconstruction.
papers.how: Uses DINOv2-informed uncertainty to remove dynamics and guide dense bundle adjustment and Gaussian optimization.
papers.what: Improves robust monocular Gaussian SLAM in changing scenes.
papers.transfer: Uncertainty-aware mapping could be repurposed for moving dust, shadows, manipulator arms, or other non-static rover observations.
papers.limitation: Its dynamic-scene assumptions differ from illumination-driven and dust-driven planetary nonstationarity.

papers.title: MASt3R-SLAM: Real-Time Dense SLAM with 3D Reconstruction Priors
papers.why: Monocular dense SLAM remains brittle when camera calibration and appearance are uncontrolled.
papers.how: Builds tracking, local fusion, loop closure, and global optimization around learned MASt3R pointmap priors.
papers.what: Produces globally consistent dense geometry in real time from uncalibrated monocular video.
papers.transfer: A strong candidate backbone for rover mapping when calibration drifts or cameras differ across missions.
papers.limitation: The learned prior is trained largely on terrestrial imagery and does not model planetary photometry or metric-scale uncertainty explicitly.

papers.title: SLAM3R: Real-Time Dense Scene Reconstruction from Monocular RGB Videos
papers.why: Optimization-heavy dense reconstruction limits real-time deployment and accumulates pipeline errors.
papers.how: Uses feed-forward multi-view local reconstruction, learned local-to-world alignment, and historical frame retrieval.
papers.what: Achieves online dense reconstruction without explicitly solving camera parameters and reports real-time operation.
papers.transfer: Useful for testing an onboard feed-forward reconstruction path before adding planetary adaptation and uncertainty heads.
papers.limitation: Its own analysis notes weaker camera localization and no global bundle adjustment; planetary long traverses may amplify both issues.

papers.title: Fast3R: Towards 3D Reconstruction of 1000+ Images in One Forward Pass
papers.why: Pairwise pointmap pipelines scale poorly to long image sequences.
papers.how: Processes many views jointly with a transformer and removes pairwise global post-processing.
papers.what: Scales feed-forward pointmap reconstruction to more than one thousand images.
papers.transfer: Relevant to long rover traverses and orbital-to-ground image collections when a global batch is available.
papers.limitation: Large joint attention and batch assumptions still challenge memory-limited onboard streaming operation.

papers.title: OmniVGGT: Omni-Modality Driven Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
papers.why: RGB-only geometry models ignore depth, calibration, and pose cues already available on robots.
papers.how: Adds a lightweight GeoAdapter and stochastic modality-subset training to inject arbitrary geometric inputs into VGGT.
papers.what: Improves geometry tasks with auxiliary modalities and transfers the representation to robotic action models.
papers.transfer: Matches planetary multisensor stacks where stereo, sparse LiDAR, IMU-derived poses, and orbital priors appear intermittently.
papers.limitation: The paper does not establish robustness to lunar reflectance, dust, radiation-induced sensor faults, or strict onboard budgets.

papers.title: QVGGT: Post-Training Quantized Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
papers.why: VGGT-scale geometry models are too large for many mobile and embedded platforms.
papers.how: Uses block-sensitivity-aware mixed precision plus camera-token filtering and compensation during calibration.
papers.what: Provides a post-training route to compress a large visual-geometry transformer.
papers.transfer: Offers a concrete onboard deployment path for a lunar-adapted geometry foundation model.
papers.limitation: Quantization calibration on terrestrial data may not preserve rare planetary illumination and low-texture failure cases.

papers.title: LiteVGGT: Boosting Vanilla VGGT via Geometry-aware Cached Token Merging
papers.why: Long-sequence geometry transformers incur redundant token computation and memory use.
papers.how: Merges tokens according to geometric importance and reuses merge decisions across adjacent layers.
papers.what: Accelerates VGGT and enables thousand-image processing with reduced memory.
papers.transfer: Can be combined with submaps for resource-aware rover reconstruction over long traverses.
papers.limitation: Token merging may discard small hazards or weakly textured geological features that matter more than average reconstruction metrics reveal.

papers.title: Neural 3D Reconstruction of Planetary Surfaces from Descent-Phase Wide-Angle Imagery
papers.why: Descent cameras have radial distortion, weak parallax, and nadir-biased motion that break conventional MVS.
papers.how: Introduces a neural height-field prior tailored to continuous planetary terrain and evaluates on simulated lunar and Martian descents.
papers.what: Shows neural reconstruction can expand coverage while maintaining useful terrain accuracy under descent geometry.
papers.transfer: Provides a bridge from descent imagery to landing-zone DEMs and rover initial maps.
papers.limitation: Evidence is simulation-centered and does not yet close the gap to real descent imagery or downstream navigation outcomes.

papers.title: Certifiably-Correct Mapping for Safe Navigation Despite Odometry Drift
papers.why: A visually detailed map can still be unsafe when odometry uncertainty corrupts obstacle locations.
papers.how: Deflates locally safe regions using incremental odometry error and adapts safe-flight-corridor and signed-distance-field maps.
papers.what: Provides formal obstacle-free guarantees and rover experiments where baselines collide but the method stops safely.
papers.transfer: Turns reconstruction uncertainty into a planning constraint suitable for high-consequence planetary autonomy.
papers.limitation: Guarantees depend on valid error bounds and local map assumptions that must be calibrated under planetary sensing failure modes.

papers.title: Learned Perceptive Forward Dynamics Model for Safe and Platform-aware Robotic Navigation
papers.why: Hand-tuned traversability costs do not capture platform-specific terrain interaction and failure risk.
papers.how: Learns forward dynamics from geometry and proprioceptive history, then plans with MPPI and predicted failure probability.
papers.what: Demonstrates safer rough-terrain navigation and sim-to-real transfer on ANYmal.
papers.transfer: Suggests conditioning rover planning on both reconstructed terrain and online wheel-soil response.
papers.limitation: Legged rigid-terrain dynamics differ from wheel-regolith interaction and low-gravity mobility.

papers.title: Verti-Bench: A General and Scalable Off-Road Mobility Benchmark for Vertically Challenging Terrain
papers.why: Static perception datasets cannot evaluate interactive vehicle-terrain mobility failures.
papers.how: Benchmarks navigation across scalable high-fidelity multiphysics environments with rigid and deformable terrain.
papers.what: Provides an interaction-based benchmark for rugged off-road mobility rather than image-only perception.
papers.transfer: A template for a lunar mobility benchmark coupling terrain geometry, regolith parameters, energy, slip, and safety.
papers.limitation: Its terrain and vehicle distributions are terrestrial and need low-gravity, regolith, illumination, and sensor extensions.

papers.title: Meta-Learning Online Dynamics Model Adaptation in Off-Road Autonomous Driving
papers.why: Fixed learned dynamics models fail when vehicle-terrain interaction changes online.
papers.how: Meta-learns adaptation bases and parameters, then updates the dynamics model online with a Kalman-filter scheme for control.
papers.what: Improves prediction, control, and safety on a real off-road vehicle across unseen terrain.
papers.transfer: Provides a mechanism for updating lunar terramechanics parameters from rover proprioception during traversal.
papers.limitation: The method needs adaptation observations and safety envelopes that may be scarce during irreversible planetary failures.

papers.title: CraterGrader: Autonomous Robotic Terrain Manipulation for Lunar Site Preparation and Earthmoving
papers.why: Lunar infrastructure requires autonomous site preparation under unknown deformable-terrain properties and no GPS.
papers.how: Closes online terrain mapping, energy-aware material transport planning, localization, and coordinated drive-tool control.
papers.what: Demonstrates autonomous lunar-like grading and smoothing as an integrated field-robot system.
papers.transfer: A systems anchor for evaluating whether reconstruction and simulation actually improve planetary worksite outcomes.
papers.limitation: Published in July 2024, it sits just outside the exact 24-month window and analogue tests cannot reproduce lunar gravity or vacuum.

papers.title: Landmark-aware autonomous odometry correction and map pruning for planetary rovers
papers.why: Long planetary traverses need drift correction without retaining an unbounded dense map.
papers.how: Selects salient terrain landmarks, represents them with NeRF, corrects odometry photometrically, and prunes the local map.
papers.what: Connects neural rendering to rover relocalization and map maintenance in simulations and experiments.
papers.transfer: A direct precursor to uncertainty-aware radiance-field submaps for long-duration rover navigation.
papers.limitation: Photometric correction can be fragile under shadow, exposure, dust, and seasonal illumination change; broad mission-data validation is still needed.

papers.title: High-fidelity 3D reconstruction for planetary exploration
papers.why: Planetary robots need dense, radiometrically rich maps from sparse rover observations and ROS data streams.
papers.how: Combines COLMAP, Nerfstudio, NeRF/3DGS, and a ROS2-compatible rosbag workflow.
papers.what: Packages geometric and neural reconstruction into an automated planetary-robotics pipeline.
papers.transfer: Useful engineering baseline for testing geometry-versus-rendering-versus-onboard-compute tradeoffs on analogue data.
papers.limitation: Evidence is pipeline-oriented; rigorous mission-scale benchmarks, uncertainty calibration, and planning impact remain open.

papers.title: Passivity-Based Tracking Control of a Planetary Rover With Robotic Arm
papers.why: Planetary mobile manipulation couples nonholonomic rover motion and arm dynamics under strict stability requirements.
papers.how: Uses passivity-based whole-body tracking control with implicit coordination of rover and manipulator.
papers.what: Provides a control-oriented treatment of a rover-arm system for planetary tasks.
papers.transfer: Creates an endpoint for digital twins whose terrain and reconstruction uncertainty must propagate into whole-body control.
papers.limitation: The paper is primarily a control contribution and does not itself solve perception, terrain estimation, or sim-to-real calibration.

papers.title: Emergent Outlier View Rejection in Visual Geometry Grounded Transformers
papers.why: Feed-forward reconstruction models can fail when image collections contain non-overlapping or irrelevant views.
papers.how: Probes internal VGGT layers, identifies emergent distractor separation, and uses it for rejection without extra training.
papers.what: Shows that a learned geometry backbone contains an exploitable noise-filtering representation.
papers.transfer: Useful for long robot image streams containing dust-obscured, overexposed, repeated, or non-overlapping frames.
papers.limitation: Synthetic and in-the-wild distractors do not cover all safety-critical sensor corruption patterns.

papers.title: Multi-view Reconstruction via SfM-guided Monocular Depth Estimation
papers.why: Multi-view matching can be unreliable while monocular foundation priors lack cross-view consistency.
papers.how: Uses sparse SfM points to guide a diffusion-based monocular depth model and produce consistent multi-view depth.
papers.what: Combines classical sparse geometry with learned image priors for diverse real-world reconstruction.
papers.transfer: A strong hybrid baseline for low-texture planetary scenes where a few reliable matches survive.
papers.limitation: Performance depends on obtaining a usable SfM scaffold; the failure mode may be severe under weak texture and repetitive terrain.

papers.title: G3R: Gradient Guided Generalizable Reconstruction
papers.why: Per-scene neural rendering is slow, while one-shot generalizable reconstruction sacrifices scene fidelity.
papers.how: Learns to iteratively update a 3D representation using differentiable-rendering gradient feedback.
papers.what: Bridges feed-forward priors and per-scene optimization for faster large-scene reconstruction.
papers.transfer: Suggests rapid analogue-site or worksite digital-twin creation without abandoning test-time correction.
papers.limitation: Evidence focuses on urban driving and drone scenes rather than low-texture or extreme-illumination terrain.

papers.title: Demonstrating DVS: Dynamic Virtual-Real Simulation Platform for Mobile Robotic Tasks
papers.why: Static, task-isolated simulators do not support dynamic agents or bidirectional virtual-real updates.
papers.how: Combines editable dynamic scenes, annotated multimodal data, motion capture, ROS, and synchronized virtual-real agents.
papers.what: Supports navigation, prediction, relocalization, grasping, and virtual-real feedback in one platform.
papers.transfer: A software-architecture reference for continuously synchronized planetary analogue digital twins.
papers.limitation: Indoor pedestrians and manipulation dominate; deformable terrain, low gravity, dust, and planetary photometry are absent.

papers.title: An efficient computational framework for the dynamics simulation of elastic wheels on deformable terrain
papers.why: Full high-fidelity wheel-soil simulation is too costly for system-level lunar rover design.
papers.how: Uses a reduced-order elastic wheel, extended terramechanics over a deformed contact patch, and partitioned integration.
papers.what: Balances transient compliant-wheel fidelity and computational efficiency, with soil-bin and rover-model validation.
papers.transfer: Suitable as a middle-fidelity layer between DEM/SPH truth models and real-time planning simulators.
papers.limitation: Validity remains tied to calibrated operating conditions and specific wheel/terrain parameter ranges.

papers.title: Granular Scaling Laws for accurate prediction of wheel mobility on slopes in low-gravity environments
papers.why: Earth-gravity tests must be translated to low-gravity slope mobility without assuming naive load equivalence.
papers.how: Extends granular scaling laws and validates transformations across slope, angular velocity, and transient slip regimes using DEM.
papers.what: Provides a quantitative route from accessible tests to low-gravity wheel-mobility prediction.
papers.transfer: Can anchor uncertainty-aware fidelity transfer between terrestrial analogue tests and lunar simulation.
papers.limitation: Scaling-law validity remains bounded by material, geometry, and modeled regimes; it is not a universal replacement for low-gravity tests.

papers.title: Navigation World Models
papers.why: Fixed navigation policies cannot easily evaluate new constraints or allocate more computation to hard decisions.
papers.how: Trains an action-conditioned diffusion transformer on human and robot egocentric video to imagine and rank trajectories.
papers.what: Uses a learned visual world model for planning in familiar and unfamiliar environments.
papers.transfer: Inspires predictive planning under communication delay, but needs geometry and physics grounding for planetary safety.
papers.limitation: Pixel-level plausibility does not guarantee metric, contact, or collision correctness.

papers.title: RLDG: Robotic Generalist Policy Distillation via Reinforcement Learning
papers.why: Generalist robot policies depend strongly on the state and action coverage of their fine-tuning data.
papers.how: Uses task-specific reinforcement learning to generate high-quality data and distills it into a generalist policy.
papers.what: Improves precise real-world manipulation and generalization over human-demonstration fine-tuning.
papers.transfer: Suggests using simulation experts to generate rare planetary recovery and contingency behaviors.
papers.limitation: Manipulation benchmarks and dense interaction data differ from sparse, safety-limited field robotics.

papers.title: ASAP: Aligning Simulation and Real-World Physics for Learning Agile Humanoid Whole-Body Skills
papers.why: System identification and domain randomization do not fully eliminate simulator dynamics mismatch.
papers.how: Learns a residual action model from real rollouts, inserts it into simulation, and fine-tunes the policy against aligned dynamics.
papers.what: Improves agile whole-body sim-to-real transfer across simulator and real-hardware settings.
papers.transfer: The residual-alignment pattern can correct rover simulator errors using limited analogue or mission telemetry.
papers.limitation: Residual actions may hide rather than identify physical causes, weakening extrapolation to unseen planetary conditions.

papers.title: SpatialVLA: Exploring Spatial Representations for Visual-Language-Action Models
papers.why: Generalist VLA policies often lack explicit spatial structure and cross-robot action representations.
papers.how: Injects ego-centric 3D position encoding and adaptive discretized action grids into a VLA model.
papers.what: Improves spatial action reasoning and adaptation across simulated and real robot setups.
papers.transfer: Useful for rover-arm tasks where object-, rover-, and world-centric frames must coexist.
papers.limitation: Existing evaluations emphasize manipulation rather than long-horizon field navigation or planetary semantics.

papers.title: Differentiable GPU-Parallelized Task and Motion Planning
papers.why: Long-horizon robot tasks require coupled discrete choices and continuous, constrained motions.
papers.how: Uses GPU-parallel seed generation and differentiable optimization inside a bilevel task-and-motion planner.
papers.what: Solves constrained TAMP problems quickly and validates on multiple real robots.
papers.transfer: Relevant to planetary construction and sample-handling sequences with coupled rover and arm decisions.
papers.limitation: Fast optimization still relies on accurate geometry, dynamics, and constraint models supplied by upstream systems.

papers.title: Scal3R: Learning Efficient Multi-Relative Pose Query for Scalable Online 3D Reconstruction
papers.why: Long online sequences can retain locally useful depth while global poses drift when every frame is regressed against one fixed anchor.
papers.how: Adds lightweight multi-reference pose-query tokens to a frozen reconstruction backbone and combines keyframes, pose-graph optimization, and loop closure.
papers.what: Reports over 60% lower average KITTI ATE than its online baseline and evaluates across driving, dynamic, indoor, and localization datasets.
papers.transfer: A direct mechanism for fixed-backbone, long-sequence reconstruction when global consistency rather than local geometry is the main failure.
papers.limitation: ECCV acceptance is confirmed by the official conference list, which remains preliminary pending publisher checks; reported gains still need independent reproduction and memory-latency profiling.

papers.title: On-the-Fly3R: Towards Robust Online 3D Reconstruction with Feed-Forward 3R Models for Large-Scale UAV Scenarios
papers.why: Existing streaming reconstruction often assumes ordered, overlapping video and therefore breaks on weakly ordered cross-strip aerial image streams.
papers.how: Uses retrieval-built dynamic subsets, a validation-rejection-retry gate before integration, and retrieval loop closures for pose-graph optimization.
papers.what: Reports training-free scaling of several feed-forward backbones beyond 5,000 images over square-kilometre UAV scenes.
papers.transfer: The reject-before-integrate pattern is useful for large planetary traverses, descent imagery, and other sparse-overlap collections.
papers.limitation: It is an unreviewed submission; robustness claims are limited to the tested UAV benchmarks and do not yet cover planetary photometry or onboard compute.

papers.title: VI3: Grounding Pretrained 3D Foundation Models with Inertial Cues
papers.why: Monocular visual geometry models cannot directly observe metric scale, while practical platforms already carry inertial sensors.
papers.how: Preintegrates IMU motion and applies architecture-adapted anchoring to recover metric scale for frozen 3D foundation-model outputs.
papers.what: Reports unsupervised metric anchoring on synthetic and real aerial data while preserving the visual model's relative geometry.
papers.transfer: Suggests a lightweight route to metric planetary reconstruction, provided low-gravity dynamics, timing, bias, and excitation are modeled explicitly.
papers.limitation: Evidence is limited to aerial datasets; observability under low excitation, bias drift, asynchronous sensing, and lunar or Martian gravity is unresolved.

papers.title: VOIM: Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Instance Mapping for RGB-D and Monocular SLAM
papers.why: Online semantic maps often make brittle instance and label commitments at first sight, when visual evidence is weakest.
papers.how: Accumulates soft off-the-shelf perception evidence per voxel across views and delays instance and label decisions.
papers.what: Reports gains over OVO-SLAM on ScanNet++ and an unchanged monocular deployment on Replica, while exposing label- and drift-limited regimes.
papers.transfer: A strong design pattern for queryable robot maps that must revise beliefs as new views arrive.
papers.limitation: Labeling is not real time, building-scale performance is drift-limited, and all evidence comes from indoor benchmarks rather than field deployment.

papers.title: GIFT: Guided Intermediate Feature Training via Action-Oriented Structural Supervision for Robotic Manipulation
papers.why: Rich visual or predictive features may retain irrelevant appearance while omitting geometry, affordance, and goal structure required for action.
papers.how: Constrains intermediate representations with geometry alignment, affordance prediction, and goal-region reconstruction across VLA and world-action model variants.
papers.what: Reports consistent zero-shot gains on LIBERO-Plus and RoboCasa, with larger benefits for articulated objects and precise real-world manipulation.
papers.transfer: Provides a testable way to make robot vision task-sufficient without tying the representation to one action decoder.
papers.limitation: All headline numbers are author-reported preprint results; causal attribution among the three supervision signals and long-horizon robustness remain open.

papers.title: WISE: World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.why: World-model rollouts are expensive and become unreliable over long horizons, so using imagination everywhere can harm policy training.
papers.how: Invokes bounded multi-view imagined rollouts only at interaction-relevant states and converts relative predicted outcomes into policy supervision.
papers.what: Reports improvements for two VLA backbones with about 80% less GPU time than full imagination plus real-world distribution-shift tests.
papers.transfer: Motivates confidence-bounded visual prediction budgets for resource-limited embodied agents.
papers.limitation: It remains a preprint, focuses on manipulation, and does not establish that visually plausible imagined outcomes are metrically or physically correct.

papers.title: FIRE3D: Feed-forward Interactive 3D Scene Reconstruction Within A Minute
papers.why: Rendering-ready radiance fields do not automatically provide separable, complete objects suitable for editing, collision, or interaction.
papers.how: A feed-forward network converts estimated posed RGB-D observations into per-object 6-DoF poses, boxes, amodally completed meshes, and textures without test-time optimization.
papers.what: Reports sub-minute scene asset generation with competitive pose, geometry-completeness, and texture results.
papers.transfer: Moves rapid reconstruction evaluation from novel-view quality toward interaction-ready assets for simulation and embodied tasks.
papers.limitation: It is an unreviewed preprint; visual completeness does not establish watertight meshes, correct physical properties, or reliable contact behavior.

papers.title: LightSplat: Real-Time High-Fidelity 3D Gaussian SLAM with Loop Closure
papers.why: 3D Gaussian SLAM must jointly sustain fast tracking, dense map quality, and global consistency under practical camera motion.
papers.how: Combines sparse-feature tracking, dual-thread Gaussian submaps, feature-accelerated 3DGS registration, loop closure, and pose-graph optimization.
papers.what: Reports near-state-of-the-art reconstruction quality and an average 8 FPS across datasets and a robotic platform.
papers.transfer: A concrete hybrid architecture for real-time dense maps that retain classical global SLAM constraints.
papers.limitation: IROS status is author-stated pending official proceedings, and robustness under harsh illumination, missing depth, and onboard compute remains unverified.

papers.title: Learning Global Camera Poses from Noisy View-Graphs for Structure from Motion
papers.why: Noisy pairwise poses and variable view-graph density make globally consistent camera estimation a bottleneck in large SfM pipelines.
papers.how: Uses a permutation-equivariant edge-conditioned graph network trained by relative-pose consistency, followed by triangulation and robust bundle adjustment.
papers.what: Reports scaling beyond one thousand images, improved registration over deep track-centric methods, and competitive accuracy with classical pipelines.
papers.transfer: Reintroduces explicit global graph reasoning into learned reconstruction without discarding geometric refinement.
papers.limitation: ECCV acceptance is confirmed by the official conference list, which remains preliminary pending publisher checks; planetary lighting, repetitive terrain, and severe graph corruption remain untested.

papers.title: Digital Twin Models for Space Robotics: Objectives, Applications, and Challenges
papers.why: Space-robotics digital twins use inconsistent definitions, objectives, lifecycle coverage, and validation evidence.
papers.how: Systematically reviews and codes 46 academic publications by objectives, applications, architecture concerns, and validation maturity.
papers.what: Identifies recurring gaps in accuracy and uncertainty, data synchronization, interoperability, reference architectures, and field-level validation.
papers.transfer: Provides an evidence taxonomy for distinguishing offline simulation, digital shadows, bidirectional twins, and predictive closed-loop systems.
papers.limitation: The evidence map covers published academic work, not unreported industrial or mission systems, and a review does not itself validate a reference architecture.

papers.title: mjorbit: A Simulation Framework for Space Robotics
papers.why: General robot simulators do not natively couple orbital propagation, spacecraft dynamics, actuators, sensors, and multibody contact at scale.
papers.how: Extends MuJoCo with space-specific dynamics and exposes low-latency CPU and high-throughput GPU backends through a Python API.
papers.what: Reports realistic on-orbit servicing, assembly, and manufacturing case studies with MPC and reinforcement-learning demonstrations.
papers.transfer: A reproducible platform for studying simulation fidelity and throughput in contact-rich space robotics.
papers.limitation: ISPARO status is author-stated, validation breadth is unclear from the abstract, and the framework does not model lunar or Martian regolith interaction.

papers.title: Data-Driven Terramechanics Approach Towards a Realistic Real-Time Simulator for Lunar Rovers
papers.why: High-fidelity continuum rover-regolith simulation is too slow for real-time testing and large learning sweeps.
papers.how: Learns a real-time terramechanics surrogate from Chrono Continuum Representation Model simulation data.
papers.what: Reports a path toward real-time prediction of lunar-rover wheel-soil interaction quantities.
papers.transfer: Can serve as a middle-fidelity layer for onboard planning, digital twins, and uncertainty-aware simulator routing.
papers.limitation: This is a preprint and the evidence is primarily simulation-to-simulation; applicability beyond training conditions and real regolith remains unresolved.

papers.title: Functional-SLAM: Interaction-Aware Mapping with Online Functional Scene Graphs
papers.why: Metric and semantic maps often omit object-to-interaction-element relations needed for fine-grained robot tasks.
papers.how: Maintains an online functional scene graph as SLAM state, commits functional edges after multi-frame evidence, and uses topology to supplement visual loop closure.
papers.what: Reports efficient online functional mapping, competitive accuracy, and improved pose estimation in repetitive or texture-degraded scenes.
papers.transfer: Connects persistent visual mapping to task-relevant function without making the robot mechanism the research contribution.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; open-vocabulary transfer, dynamic-scene behavior, edge rollback, and building-scale stability remain unclear.

papers.title: FARM: Reading Failure Signals from the Internal Predictive States of a Frozen Robotic World Model
papers.why: Predictive robot world models may encode impending failure internally without exposing a calibrated online risk signal.
papers.how: Trains a 33,985-parameter readout on frozen VLA-JEPA predictive states for stepwise failure and trajectory-level causal risk.
papers.what: Reports stronger simulated and real-robot failure detection than external visual or action monitors with about 0.2256 ms extra latency after state computation.
papers.transfer: Turns a frozen visual world model into a lightweight risk sensor for task monitoring and selective intervention.
papers.limitation: All results are author-reported preprint evidence; the readout may learn task progress or benchmark-specific failure patterns rather than transferable causality.

papers.title: Localized Visual Feature Aggregation via Focus Pooling for Visuomotor Policies
papers.why: Global pooling can dilute local control-relevant visual cues, while input cropping hard-codes the focus mechanism.
papers.how: Uses proprioceptive context to attention-pool intermediate CNN features and trains only a small fraction of encoder parameters.
papers.what: Reports 36.2% and 41.2% success-rate gains over pooling and explicit-focus methods while training 5.8% of encoder parameters.
papers.transfer: Provides a compact vision-centered mechanism for exposing local action-sufficient features in visuomotor policies.
papers.limitation: CoRL status and gains are author-stated; benefits may arise from extra proprioceptive conditioning or parameter updates rather than pooling alone.

papers.title: Monkey See, Can Monkey Do? A Benchmark for Evaluating Robot Skill Learning by Observation
papers.why: Robot learning from human video lacks a unified setup for separating algorithm progress from hardware, data, and environment differences.
papers.how: RoboReel bundles human videos, simulated trajectories, evaluation environments, ten manipulation tasks, and four test suites including visual distractors and long horizons.
papers.what: Benchmarks more than seven algorithms and reports that long-horizon and low-tolerance tasks remain challenging.
papers.transfer: A common protocol for testing visual imitation representations and robustness before real-robot deployment.
papers.limitation: CoRL status is author-stated, evaluations focus on manipulation, and benchmark ranking may not transfer across embodiments or navigation domains.

papers.title: EliGSiR: Continual RGB-D Mapping with Gaussian Splatting under Bounded Compute
papers.why: Continual RGB-D mapping needs to preserve old regions and assimilate new observations within a fixed optimization budget.
papers.how: Adapts view scheduling, supervision resolution, and Gaussian geometry growth to current map evidence and mapping load.
papers.what: Reports improved anytime and final reconstruction quality across Replica, TUM RGB-D, ScanNet++, and real RGB-D sequences under controlled budgets.
papers.transfer: A practical blueprint for resource-aware maps that remain usable throughout acquisition rather than only after offline optimization.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint centered on indoor RGB-D; long outdoor trajectories, monocular input, severe illumination, and onboard power remain untested.

papers.title: AMB3R-SLAM: Kilometer-scale SLAM with Hierarchical Backend
papers.why: Real-time monocular reconstruction over ten-thousand-frame and kilometer-scale trajectories requires both low-latency tracking and global consistency.
papers.how: Couples a lightweight front end with a hierarchical backend that progressively enforces local, mid-level, and global consistency and can accept stereo, RGB-D, or LiDAR cues.
papers.what: Reports kilometer-scale operation on a consumer GPU and strong tracking across nine datasets, including more than 70% ATE reductions on two benchmarks.
papers.transfer: Shows how hierarchical consistency can scale learned dense SLAM toward long rover or UAV traverses.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; detailed memory, compute, dynamic-scene failure, and planetary-domain evidence require independent validation.

papers.title: RawSLAM: Online HDR Gaussian SLAM from Linear Radiance
papers.why: Eight-bit tone-mapped inputs discard radiometric information and can cause dense visual SLAM to fail in shadows and highlights.
papers.how: Tracks and maps on single-exposure 16-bit linear HDR using logarithmic Gaussian colors, range-compressed photometric loss, and structure-guided gradient weighting.
papers.what: Reports transfer to several Gaussian-SLAM backbones and a ten-sequence RAW, depth, IMU, and OptiTrack dataset.
papers.transfer: Makes sensor radiometry an explicit part of online reconstruction, directly relevant to extreme planetary illumination.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint with ten indoor sequences; code and data are promised but were not yet verified as publicly available.

papers.title: SplashSplat: Reconstructing Splashing Liquids from Real-World Multi-View Videos
papers.why: Fast splashing liquids are textureless, topologically changing, and too transient for standard dynamic reconstruction assumptions.
papers.how: Fuses per-frame mask-derived SDFs, transports level sets for coarse flow, and advects corrected and reseeded Lagrangian carriers that decode local Gaussians.
papers.what: Introduces a twenty-scene synchronized seven-camera benchmark and reports more plausible motion and lower training cost than dynamic Gaussian baselines.
papers.transfer: A useful stress case for observation-bounded physical priors in dynamic reconstruction and simulation-ready scene capture.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; masks and calibration are strong inputs, while quantitative real flow or material ground truth remains limited.

papers.title: Can 4D Foundation Models Remember?
papers.why: Pixel metrics cannot test whether a 4D model preserves objects, appearance, and motion after they leave the current field of view.
papers.how: PersistBench uses 360-degree video as omniscient ground truth and measures object permanence, motion continuity, and appearance preservation.
papers.what: Reports that evaluated 4D model categories retain only short-term consistency that degrades substantially after objects leave view.
papers.transfer: Creates an object-centric reliability test for long-horizon visual memory in dynamic maps and world models.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint benchmark rather than a reconstruction method, and its 360-degree capture assumptions may not represent sparse field robots.

papers.title: Fleet-To-Lab: A Transfer Learning Framework For Lunar Rover Slippage Estimation Via Model Fusion
papers.why: Earth-trained slip estimators transfer poorly to lunar terrain while mission data are scarce and distributed across heterogeneous rover embodiments.
papers.how: Fuses heterogeneous historical rover experts with AcoMerge parameter search and adapts the merged model using a modest amount of new-unit data.
papers.what: Reports improved balanced accuracy and macro-F1 against deep model-fusion baselines in high-fidelity physics simulation.
papers.transfer: Treats prior rover models as reusable mission assets for few-shot adaptation of future lunar vehicles.
papers.limitation: Conference status is author-stated and evaluation remains simulation-based; real Earth-to-Moon transfer and calibrated uncertainty are unresolved.

papers.title: SenseFuse: Label-Free Fusion of Image and Shape Encoders for Open-Vocabulary 3D Instance Segmentation
papers.why: Open-vocabulary 3D labeling overuses image features even though 2D image and 3D shape encoders make complementary mistakes.
papers.how: Selects a scene-level image-shape fusion weight by maximizing an unlabeled sensitivity measure over instance proposals.
papers.what: Reports labeling gains across ScanNet200, Replica, and ScanNet++, recovering most of the oracle-weight gain and improving AP in 21 of 22 settings.
papers.transfer: A lightweight way to exploit heterogeneous visual and geometric evidence in robot scene understanding without task labels.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; scene-level weights may miss object-level variation, and indoor dense scans do not establish sparse outdoor transfer.

papers.title: PerSeM: Persistent Semantic Memory for Long-Horizon Open-Vocabulary UAV Mapping
papers.why: Frame-wise open-vocabulary predictions remain inconsistent across long trajectories, viewpoint changes, and repeated observations.
papers.how: Associates predictions with world-space voxels and conservatively refines majority semantic memory through history preservation, trust-aware replay, and contextual verification.
papers.what: Reports improved semantic correctness and temporal stability on Forest and UAVScenes, especially in difficult unstable regions.
papers.transfer: A training-free persistent-memory design for long rover or UAV surveys where repeated evidence should revise map beliefs.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; majority memory can preserve systematic errors and depends on pose and voxel association quality.

papers.title: AnyviewMeter: Adapting Robotic Reward Models with Camera Geometry and Multi-View Attention
papers.why: A visual reward model can change its progress estimate with camera viewpoint and occlusion even when task state is unchanged.
papers.how: Combines low-rank adaptation, token-aligned Plucker rays, and synchronous multi-view block attention in a pretrained scalar reward model.
papers.what: Reports reduced progress error in simulated and real manipulation relative to RGB fine-tuning and averaging independent view predictions.
papers.transfer: Makes camera geometry explicit in task-state evaluation, supporting view-robust visual monitoring and active camera selection.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; scalar reward correlation does not prove causal task understanding or safety under unseen tasks and cameras.

papers.title: FunArt: Decoding Functional Structure and Articulation from Generative 3D Latents
papers.why: Robots need movable parts, functional interaction elements, and kinematics before contact, while static scans usually separate these outputs.
papers.how: Converts reconstructed RGB-D instances into a frozen TRELLIS.2 latent prior and decodes movable parts, functional elements, and joint type, axis, origin, and range.
papers.what: Reports state-of-the-art Articulate3D results and end-to-end gains across movable-part, articulation, and functional-element metrics.
papers.transfer: Turns generative 3D latents into an actionable structural prior for task-oriented robot perception.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint evaluated from a single static configuration on one main benchmark; closed-loop interaction and state tracking remain unproven.

papers.title: Towards Practical Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.why: Practical 3DGS compression needs small models without complex spatial context or platform-dependent entropy-decoding failures.
papers.how: Uses anchor-wise causal factorization, compact linear context models, rate-distortion training, adaptive pruning, quantization-aware training, and integer context inference.
papers.what: Reports state-of-the-art compression among the compared methods with fast decoding and bit-exact cross-platform symbol consistency.
papers.transfer: Makes compressed 3D maps reproducibly decodable between onboard and ground hardware rather than optimizing rate and image quality alone.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; hardware diversity, energy, difficult geometry, and the claimed rate-distortion frontier require independent reproduction.

papers.title: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations
papers.why: Point trackers normally trade long temporal horizons against dense coverage, while repeated observations cause redundant scene state.
papers.how: Represents video as persistent world-coordinate 3D tracks, de-duplicates sliding-window states by voxelization, separates endpoint and trajectory refinement, and samples features with 3D WAFT.
papers.what: Reports dense tracking beyond one thousand frames within 40 GB and more than twenty APD points over open all-frame dense trackers on short TAPVid-3D clips.
papers.transfer: A persistent identity-and-geometry substrate for long-horizon dynamic maps, object memory, and selective downstream semantics.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint and a tracker rather than a metrically complete mapper; topology changes, merge errors, and low-texture planetary transfer remain unresolved.

papers.title: OceanXL: Large-scale Underwater 3D Gaussian Splatting via Block Partitioning and Adaptive Pruning
papers.venue: arXiv; SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 stated by authors
papers.why: Large underwater reconstructions combine adverse image formation with 3DGS memory and optimization growth.
papers.how: Partitions scenes into spatially coherent blocks for divide-and-conquer optimization and prunes redundant primitives with an underwater-adaptive rule.
papers.what: Reports favorable scalability and compactness on five large scenes and introduces a large-scale underwater dataset.
papers.transfer: A transferable large-scene design for extreme-medium reconstruction where local budgets must preserve global geometry.
papers.limitation: Venue status is author-stated; cross-block geometry, dataset release, and transfer outside underwater imagery require verification.

papers.title: Efficient Continuous DEM Reconstruction under Limited Target-Resolution Supervision
papers.why: High-resolution terrain supervision is scarce, and dense output queries can make continuous DEM reconstruction computationally expensive.
papers.how: Predicts low-resolution coefficient fields, reuses local Fourier residual functions, and fuses basis evaluations with geometry guidance.
papers.what: Reports roughly twelve percent lower land RMSE and MAE than bicubic at an unseen three-times scale while nine-times output density adds about two percent MACs.
papers.transfer: A compact continuously queryable terrain representation for multi-scale rover mapping and constrained map transmission.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint operating from existing DEMs; super-resolution cannot create independently observed fine geometry and planetary transfer is untested.

papers.title: X2Real: an eXtensive simulation benchmark for real-world generalist policies
papers.why: Simulation benchmarks can mis-rank real robot policies because of fidelity gaps, narrow task coverage, and training-test leakage.
papers.how: Calibrates visual and physical properties in Isaac Lab-Arena, defines ten capability dimensions and forty-four tasks, separates train and evaluation pipelines, and applies multi-axis randomization.
papers.what: Reports a 0.84 linear correlation between simulated and real evaluations and provides nearly three hundred hours of annotated simulated trajectories.
papers.transfer: A governance and validation template for testing whether planetary simulation predicts real analogue-field system rankings.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; the reported correlation may be specific to selected tasks, hardware, policies, and calibration data.

papers.title: ForceTwin: Physics-informed Digital Twins for Robotic Manipulation from Instrumented Human Interaction
papers.why: Kinematic or appearance-derived twins miss inertia, friction, damping, and state-dependent mechanism forces that determine manipulation effort.
papers.how: Identifies articulation, parametric dynamics, and a structured neural force residual from synchronized human-probing poses and forces.
papers.what: Reports nearly halved inertial-parameter error and 87 percent goal completion across nine object-embodiment pairs, versus 60 and 57 percent for two baselines.
papers.transfer: Suggests an interaction-updated physical-twin pattern for wheel-regolith parameters and other hidden planetary contact properties.
papers.limitation: It is a manipulation preprint requiring instrumented probing; low-gravity granular media, persistent synchronization, and safe exploration remain untested.

papers.title: Learning to Drive on Mars: Visual Multimodal Traversability Estimation for Off-World Navigation
papers.why: Learning-based Martian navigation lacks large real mission datasets spanning diverse terrain, lighting, vehicle state, and slip.
papers.how: Aligns Perseverance stereo imagery, poses, accelerometry, rocker-bogie angles, tilt, and slip estimates across five hundred sols and forty-five kilometers, then learns uncertainty-aware traversability.
papers.what: Reports AUROC 0.874 and F1 0.758, improvements of 0.058 and 0.156 over the strongest compared baseline, plus ENav and physical test-bed integration.
papers.transfer: A rare real Mars visual-mobility substrate for uncertainty calibration, strict geographic splits, and simulation validation.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint and its code and dataset were only promised; operational selection bias, label quality, and unseen-site closed-loop safety remain unresolved.

papers.title: SplatLabel: Pseudo-Labelling through 4D Gaussian Splatting
papers.why: Dynamic 3D semantic pseudo-labels need temporal consistency, geometry in unobserved regions, and calibrated abstention rather than heuristic fusion.
papers.how: Tracks primitive trajectories and lifetimes in 4D Gaussians, adds LiDAR-derived virtual depth and distilled soft semantics, and evaluates generalized risk-recall.
papers.what: Reports stronger SemanticKITTI segmentation and occupancy pseudo-labeling than the compared methods across multiple recall levels.
papers.transfer: A selective 4D semantic-map mechanism that can expose when a robot should trust or reject generated labels.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint validated on one main benchmark and assumes 360-degree LiDAR; calibration under sparse sensing and domain shift is unknown.

papers.title: Retrieve-to-Localize: Bridging Large Language Models and LiDAR Geometry for Spatial Grounding
papers.why: Outdoor robots need to compose spatial relations and return precise target coordinates rather than only detect objects or answer in text.
papers.how: Aligns LiDAR point features with an LLM, retrieves language-conditioned position-aware proposals, and refines coordinates from local points.
papers.what: Reports substantial coordinate-prediction gains over representative LiDAR-language and multi-camera vision-language baselines on SpatialLiDAR-QA.
papers.transfer: Constrains language reasoning with local geometry for task-executable spatial queries in 3D maps.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint with code and data only promised; benchmark coordinate error does not establish open-world or closed-loop task success.

papers.title: Know-Your-Scene (KYS)-SLAM: Hierarchical Semantic-Motion Priors for Feature Matching in Stereo Visual SLAM
papers.why: Binary rejection of semantically ambiguous or dynamic features suppresses outliers but can remove geometric support needed by bundle adjustment.
papers.how: Continuously modulates ORB-SLAM3 correspondence costs with semantic class, panoptic identity, and a training-free depth-aware motion score while keeping the backend unchanged.
papers.what: Reports ATE improvements under one fixed configuration across KITTI, EuRoC, dynamic driving, and synthetic sequences without per-dataset retuning.
papers.transfer: A modular way to inject vision semantics and motion evidence into geometric localization without replacing the established optimizer.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint dependent on upstream segmentation and flow; low-texture, extreme-illumination, and planetary cases remain untested.

papers.title: PointCast: One World Model for Rigid, Articulated, and Deformable Object Manipulation
papers.why: Manipulation world models need an inspectable state representation that can span rigid, articulated, and deformable objects.
papers.how: Uses identity-preserving object and end-effector point sets with a diffusion transformer, alternating local and global attention and conditioning on commanded end-effector motion.
papers.what: Reports first place in three of four simulated regimes, competitive real teleoperation prediction, and sampling-based MPC performance.
papers.transfer: A point-level visual and geometric world-model substrate for action prediction, uncertainty localization, and task planning.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint using separate checkpoints by regime; unified cross-material generalization, visibility, and long-rollout calibration are unresolved.

papers.title: Imagine then Verify: Affordance-Targeted Active Perception for Task-Oriented Grasping in Cluttered Scenes
papers.why: Task-relevant affordance regions are often occluded, while full-object reconstruction spends viewpoint budget on irrelevant surfaces.
papers.how: Generates complete-shape and affordance hypotheses, then selects views by expected hypothesis-entropy reduction and real-observation affordance verification gain.
papers.what: Reports higher functional-grasp success in simulated and real clutter and more than fifty-seven percent fewer views than reconstruction-based active perception.
papers.transfer: Turns active vision from scene completeness toward task-risk reduction for affordances and navigation hazards.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; a biased shape prior can focus sensing on the wrong hypothesis, and the evidence is limited to task-oriented grasping.

papers.title: ReVar3R: Gauge-Aware Perturbation Uncertainty for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
papers.why: Perturbation uncertainty for feed-forward 3D reconstruction is contaminated when repeated predictions choose different similarity gauges.
papers.how: Registers perturbed predictions into a common similarity frame before aggregating per-point variance, without retraining the reconstruction model.
papers.what: Reports lower AUSE than model-native confidence in fifteen of eighteen model-dataset conditions across VGGT, pi3, MASt3R, and six datasets.
papers.transfer: A geometry-aware uncertainty layer for deciding when active acquisition, abstention, or digital-twin updates are warranted.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint and does not detect systematic biases that remain stable across perturbations; absolute and cross-domain calibration are unresolved.

papers.title: Matisse: Active 3D Reconstruction through Evidential Uncertainty and Information Gain
papers.why: Active reconstruction needs to spend a limited view budget on genuinely missing or ambiguous geometry rather than generic coverage.
papers.how: Derives evidential uncertainty and information gain from cross-attention evidence in a pretrained generative 3D model for training-free view and keyframe selection.
papers.what: Reports Chamfer-distance reductions of 12.7, 3.8, and 9.2 percent on GSO30, YCB-V, and Replica, plus comparable quality to Stream3D with fourteen percent of the views.
papers.transfer: A foundation-model evidence signal for active rover viewing and budgeted mapping.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; the project page says code is forthcoming, and biased generative evidence may direct sensing away from real errors.

papers.title: VASC: Value-Aware Sparse Computation for Efficient Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
papers.why: Quadratic global attention limits VGGT- and pi3-class reconstruction on long sequences and resource-constrained platforms.
papers.how: Selects valuable tokens for sparse attention and uses execution-aware cross-layer memory to avoid redundant computation.
papers.what: Reports up to 2.29-times acceleration over dense VGGT and improved pose and reconstruction metrics over FasterVGGT on 7Scenes and NeuralRGB-D.
papers.transfer: A public implementation for studying task-aware compute allocation in streaming or onboard 3D reconstruction.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; embedded energy, tail latency, long-horizon drift, and robustness of the value predictor remain unverified.

papers.title: 4D-HOF: Hand-Object Flow Matching for Feed-Forward 4D Interaction Reconstruction
papers.why: Hand-object reconstruction must recover occluded motion while rejecting visually plausible but physically impossible interaction states.
papers.how: Conditions flow matching on coarse states from visual foundation models and applies test-time guidance from physical constraints and 2D evidence.
papers.what: Reports state-of-the-art out-of-distribution interaction reconstruction in the authors' comparisons.
papers.transfer: A test case for combining visual reconstruction with contact-aware constraints and uncertainty under occlusion.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint whose abstract provides limited quantitative detail; real contact validity and long interaction rollouts require replication.

papers.title: MarsLab: An Open-Source ROS2 Simulation Platform for Mars Rover Autonomy
papers.why: Mars autonomy research lacks an open task environment combining terrain, illumination, dust, multimodal sensing, and ROS2 rover interfaces.
papers.how: Builds a Perseverance-class Isaac Sim rover with HiRISE or procedural terrain, rocks, craters, solar illumination, atmospheric dust, and RGB, depth, point cloud, LiDAR, IMU, odometry, and ground truth outputs.
papers.what: Provides SLAM and visual place-recognition benchmarks across sensing, dust, geometry, route, and illumination changes, with a verified public project and code repository.
papers.transfer: A reproducible base for calibrating planetary visual simulation and testing reconstruction, localization, and navigation under controlled Mars conditions.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; iSpaRo status is author-stated, and mission-data calibration of dust, reflectance, sensor physics, and wheel-regolith interaction is not established.

papers.title: RenderBench: Benchmarking Render-to-Real Transfer with Reconstructed Editable Digital Twins
papers.why: Render-to-real studies lack paired, editable, geometrically and temporally validated digital twins that can localize transfer failures.
papers.how: Reconstructs static and dynamic real scenes and pairs real targets, editable twins, proxy renders, and annotations with geometry and time consistency screening.
papers.what: Retains twelve of fourteen candidate scenes and provides 1,496 paired real-proxy frames with failure factors for object, visibility, articulation, and motion.
papers.transfer: A validation pattern for auditing planetary sensor and scene twins instead of relying on visual realism alone.
papers.limitation: It is a small indoor-oriented preprint benchmark; its coverage cannot establish open-world or planetary digital-twin fidelity.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Driven Real2Sim2Real for 3D Object Detection
papers.why: Appearance gaps and geographic misalignment weaken the transfer of simulated driving data to real 3D perception.
papers.how: Reconstructs georeferenced paired driving digital twins, renders aligned simulation views, and uses diffusion-based Sim2Real generation and co-training.
papers.what: Reports DETR3D reaching 93.18 percent of oracle mAP without target images in detector training, while simple co-training exceeds the reported oracle.
papers.transfer: A paired, location-aligned alternative to blind domain randomization for evaluating simulation-to-perception transfer.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint in autonomous driving; data leakage, generative memorization, geographic bias, and transfer to planetary sensing require audit.

papers.title: DepthWorld: 3D World Model for Robot Manipulation
papers.why: Cross-robot video mixes cameras, kinematics, and viewpoints, while RGB-only world models lack reliable metric 3D supervision.
papers.how: Combines learned stereo depth with a joint factor graph to estimate shared robot kinematics and per-scene extrinsics, then jointly predicts multi-view RGB and metric depth with spatial latent tiling.
papers.what: The project reports 71,100 episodes from 28 robots and 13 laboratories, under 0.7-pixel reprojection error for ninety percent of external-camera episodes, and a 1.48 dB PSNR gain from depth supervision.
papers.transfer: A verified public data, calibration, and model stack for geometry-aware visual world models across robot embodiments.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint with author-stated CoRL status; visual quality and reprojection accuracy do not establish contact safety or closed-loop performance.

papers.title: Blackout vs. Freeze: Visual Failure Modes in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.why: Camera blackouts or frozen frames can trigger unsafe VLA actions that ordinary task-success metrics fail to expose.
papers.how: Injects camera blackout and freeze faults into pi0.5 and GR00T, compares proprioceptive and mitigation settings, and validates selected behaviors on real robots.
papers.what: Reports extreme joint behavior under frozen images, frequent drops after post-grasp blackout, and cases where higher success from mitigation coincides with more unintended contact.
papers.transfer: A concrete visual-fault protocol and safety metric set for robot policies and geometry-aware world models.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint over a limited model and task set; the observed failure patterns do not establish general VLA safety properties.

papers.title: World Motion Models
papers.venue: arXiv; NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight stated by authors
papers.why: Pixel and latent video models do not directly unify articulated objects, humans, hand-object interactions, cameras, and robot states for downstream planning.
papers.how: Represents entities and actions as sparse SE(3) trajectories and uses flow matching, per-token noise, and any-to-any masks for prediction and infilling.
papers.what: Demonstrates six application families including prediction, infilling, model-predictive control, inverse kinematics, retargeting, and policy use.
papers.transfer: A compositional geometric motion vocabulary for vision-conditioned embodied world models and task planning.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint with author-stated Spotlight status; long-horizon error, observation grounding, contact detail, and real closed-loop safety remain unresolved.

papers.title: AssemblyWorld: A Benchmark for Vision-Based Embodied Assembly
papers.why: Embodied benchmarks that expose mesh or simulator state cannot isolate whether an agent can infer precise assembly geometry from images.
papers.how: Provides an interactive 3D environment in which agents inspect only rendered 2D views and manipulate rigid parts across one hundred tasks and eighty objects.
papers.what: Across eight evaluated agents, the strongest reaches 80.9 percent part accuracy but only 59.4 percent complete assembly.
papers.transfer: A vision-centered test bed for multi-view part understanding, pose, active viewing, and long-horizon spatial reasoning.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint with synthetic rendering, rigid-part assumptions, and limited scale; real contact, tolerance, and material effects are absent.

papers.title: Slot3R: Set-Associative Spatial Memory for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
papers.why: Spatially close streaming observations may represent distinct surfaces, viewpoints, or visibility states, so immediate memory fusion can erase complementary evidence.
papers.how: Retrofits frozen Point3R with set-associative memory that keeps multiple states at one spatial address and a bounded sparse readout that decouples storage from per-frame access.
papers.what: Reports 57.1 to 63.1 percent lower point-cloud accuracy error on 7Scenes and 64.0 to 72.0 percent lower error on NeuralRGBD at 300 to 500 sampled frames, while completing 600 to 1000 frames near 19 FPS where two baselines run out of memory after 800 frames.
papers.transfer: A training-free memory organization principle for long-running robot reconstruction that preserves ambiguity before later evidence resolves it.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; sequences are at most one thousand sampled frames, and loop closure, dynamic identities, memory growth, and embedded performance remain unverified.

papers.title: RiCo: Neural Simulation of Rigid-Body Interactions via Local Contact Reasoning
papers.why: Scene-level neural dynamics can waste computation and lose the local surface interactions that actually exchange rigid-body contact forces.
papers.how: Reasons across sparse contact-surface neighborhoods using relative geometry, motion, and physical properties, then propagates local effects within each rigid object.
papers.what: Reports 31 to 35 percent lower 100-frame position error, about 38 percent lower orientation error, 2.22 mm mean penetration-depth difference, zero-shot scaling to 270 objects, and preliminary real multi-ball transfer.
papers.transfer: A candidate fast local-contact surrogate for multi-fidelity simulation, provided its rigid-body assumptions are explicitly relaxed and validated for terrain interaction.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint evaluated mainly on MOVi and rigid collisions; evidence does not establish granular wheel-regolith, deformable terrain, or low-gravity fidelity.

papers.title: VersaCamVLA: Camera-Configurable VLA Policies for Robotic Manipulation
papers.why: VLA manipulation policies trained with fixed camera counts and poses are brittle when deployment changes the available view set.
papers.how: Maps arbitrary posed RGB view sets into fixed-size scene tokens using multi-signal target-view prediction and wrist-augmented pose sampling, then injects them into a pretrained VLA.
papers.what: Reports consistent gains over prior VLA and direct multi-view baselines on RoboTwin, LIBERO, and a real robot under varying camera counts and unseen poses.
papers.transfer: A camera-set interface for multi-view embodied perception that can later support active view choice and fault-aware scene evidence.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint with author-stated NeurIPS status; metric geometry, calibration-noise sensitivity, visual fault handling, and artifact reproducibility remain to be independently checked.

papers.title: Rendering-Free Lookahead for Question-Guided Active Vision
papers.why: Question-guided robot vision needs to anticipate which unseen view will reveal task evidence without rendering every candidate online.
papers.how: Uses privileged 3DGS future-view rendering and a frozen VLM to create one- and two-step answerability targets, then distills a deployment policy from questions, recent views, and candidate camera actions.
papers.what: Reports a 43 percent mean-judge-score improvement over a direct-action baseline using the same VLM on 377 unseen-environment E3VS-Bench episodes.
papers.transfer: A way to amortize simulation-based visual lookahead into a low-cost active camera policy for task-directed perception.
papers.limitation: It is a preprint; VLM-judge bias, 3DGS-teacher errors, answerability calibration, and real-robot camera-motion evidence remain unresolved.
